concepts.title: Types of Movement and Muscle Types
concepts.definition: Movements in the body include amoeboid, ciliary and muscular types; muscles are of three types, skeletal or striated voluntary muscles attached to bones, smooth or non-striated involuntary muscles of visceral organs, and cardiac muscles of the heart that are striated, involuntary and interconnected by intercalated discs.
concepts.key_idea: A skeletal muscle fibre is a syncytium with sarcolemma, sarcoplasm, many nuclei and myofibrils, whose sarcomere between two Z lines is the functional contractile unit.

solution_steps.explain: Note striations, control and location of the muscle.
Identify myofibrils, sarcomeres, Z lines and intercalated discs where present.
State whether the muscle is voluntary or involuntary and its role.

concepts.title: Sliding Filament Theory of Muscle Contraction
concepts.section: 17.2.1 Structure of Contractile Proteins, 17.3 Skeletal System
concepts.definition: Muscle contraction follows the sliding filament theory: a signal from the central nervous system releases calcium ions from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, calcium binds troponin, myosin heads bind actin forming cross bridges, and actin filaments slide over myosin pulling Z lines closer, shortening the sarcomere while the filaments themselves stay the same length.
concepts.key_idea: ATP hydrolysis powers cross bridge cycling, and relaxation follows when calcium is pumped back and troponin tropomyosin complex masks the actin binding sites again.

solution_steps.explain: Trace the impulse from motor neuron to calcium release.

concepts.title: Skeletal System: Axial and Appendicular Skeleton with Joints
concepts.definition: The human skeleton of 206 bones divides into an axial skeleton of skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum with a total of 80 bones, and an appendicular skeleton of limbs and girdles with 126 bones, and joints are classified as fibrous, cartilaginous and synovial, with ball and socket, hinge, pivot, gliding and saddle types.
concepts.key_idea: Synovial joints with synovial fluid allow free movement, as in the ball and socket joint of the shoulder and the hinge joint of the knee, while skull sutures are fixed fibrous joints.

concepts.title: Disorders of Muscular and Skeletal Systems
concepts.section: 17.5 Disorders of Muscular and Skeletal Systems
concepts.definition: Common disorders include myasthenia gravis where antibodies destroy the neuromuscular junction causing fatigue, muscular dystrophy as a genetic degeneration of muscles, tetany from low calcium causing rapid spasms, arthritis as joint inflammation, gout from uric acid crystal deposition, and osteoporosis with decreased bone mass in old age.
concepts.key_idea: Each disorder maps to a component of the locomotor system: junction failure in myasthenia gravis, gene defect in muscular dystrophy, low blood calcium in tetany and uric acid crystals in gout.

Look for autoimmune, genetic, ionic or metabolic causes.
